title: Session epoch negotiation and opaque checkpoint shim for SSE resume compatibility
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an interoperable compatibility shim that allows legacy and constrained clients to resume Server-Sent Event (SSE) streams using a compact opaque checkpoint token and a lightweight epoch negotiation handshake. Goal: reduce user-visible reconnects and duplicated output while avoiding large on-client state and without changing existing streaming payload shapes for modern clients.
background: We have multiple customer reports where long-running streaming sessions (chat generation, tool-calls) fail to resume because clients cannot store or compute large resume checkpoints (full byte offsets + sequence maps) or because intermediaries (CDNs/proxies) rewrite headers. Existing resume approaches at Redwood assume clients can persist structured resume tokens with model/version/offset metadata. Some embedded clients and mobile SDKs cannot. This ticket designs a shim layer that issues small opaque tokens and negotiates 'session epochs' on reconnect to safely resume without relying on clients understanding the full resume schema.
acceptance_criteria: Server can issue a base64-opaque checkpoint token (<=128 bytes) on initial stream and include it as X-RW-Resume-Token in stream envelope
On reconnect, client may present the opaque token; server verifies HMAC & epoch and returns negotiated epoch header; resume succeeds without client-side semantic parsing
Tool/function-call boundaries are preserved: if a reconnect occurs mid-function-call, server either replays last idempotent call or returns a deterministic reconciliation event to the client
Fallback path to short-polling (non-stream) is available and documented if resume negotiation fails
End-to-end tests with simulated packet loss and proxy header-stripping show <=1% extra duplicate tokens vs baseline and mean reconnection latency < 250ms (median target)
Security review completed for token design (HMAC + rolling nonce) and KMS integration; threat mitigations documented
Feature gated behind runtime-2.3 flag and can be canaried by region/customer tier
design_decisions: Use opaque resume tokens (versioned) containing: session_id, server_epoch, short ack_window, HMAC(prefix) - payload encrypted server-side; token is base64-url encoded
Do NOT embed model state or full sequence offsets in token to keep token small and to avoid leaking model identifiers to clients/proxies
Server maintains short-lived checkpoint metadata (bounded window, TTL 24h) keyed by session_id+epoch to allow compact resume without full state replication
Epoch negotiation: client presents token; server responds with X-RW-Epoch: <epoch> header and X-RW-Resume-Status: accepted|stale|rejected
If resume is stale (server epoch advanced beyond client's window) server returns a reconciliation notification chunk with structured delta that the client can apply or fall back to a summary event

Tool/function-call safety: if reconnect boundary intersects an in-flight tool call, server emits an explicit FunctionCall-Resume marker with deterministic idempotency key so clients can dedupe or re-call safely
Tokens are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a key in KMS; signing key rotates monthly and token version encodes rotation key index
For proxies/CDN that strip headers, also emit a small inline resume meta-chunk as the first event in the stream body so clients behind stripping infrastructure can still grab the token
implementation_notes: Server: add resume token generator module that queries KMS to sign token; store checkpoint metadata in fast key-value store (redis with LRU, ttl 24h)
Server: extend SSE envelope to include optional headers X-RW-Resume-Token, X-RW-Epoch, X-RW-Resume-Status; preserve backwards compatibility by not requiring these headers for existing clients
Client SDKs: add optional compact resume support in mobile/web SDKs. Default to disabled for older SDKs; enable for new releases in runtime-2.3 canary
Edge cases: when checkpoint metadata evicted (TTL/eviction), server should return 'stale' with concise reconciliation and metric tag resume.stale=true
Integrate with existing streaming metrics (token_issued, resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_stale, resume_latency_ms)
Add deterministic function-call idempotency token generation for in-flight tool calls (derive from session_id + function_call_seq + server_epoch)
Provide HTTP 412-style handshake: client POSTs /sessions/{id}/resumekey with token to validate (used by heavy clients to pre-warm)
testing_plan: Unit tests for token generation & verification including key rotation cases
Integration test: simulate client reconnect after random delay, verify resume accepted and no duplicated function-call side effects
Chaos test: simulate header stripping (remove X-RW-Resume-Token) and validate inline resume meta-chunk resolution works
Performance test: measure resume negotiation latency under 95th percentile load; target < 500ms P95 during canary
Security test: fuzz tokens, attempt replay and tamper, verify HMAC and epoch protections prevent unauthorized resume
Interoperability test: older SDKs that ignore headers should still consume stream; new SDKs should resume properly
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Alpha): internal canary with SDK team and a couple internal apps only; runtime-2.3 flag off by default
Phase 2 (Beta): enable for 5% of hosted traffic in us-west; export detailed metrics and capture traces
Phase 3 (Gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 weeks if key metrics stable
Abort criteria: resume_success_rate < 99% or resume_stale rate > 3% or unexplained >5% increase in duplicate tool-call invocations
Post-rollout: migrate to default on new SDKs and add opt-out for legacy enterprise customers
monitoring: Alert: resume_stale_rate > 1% sustained for 15min -> pager to infra
Tracing: attach resume token id to stream traces for end-to-end latency correlation
Audit: log token-issue and salt-index for security audits (redact token in logs)
